image_description: A close-up, high-contrast image of a cooked Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) against a dark background. The crab is positioned ventral-side up or tilted, revealing the white/cream underside of the carapace and legs, while the dorsal side shows characteristic reddish-orange coloration from cooking. The large chelipeds (claws) are prominent, with red tips and white joints. Several walking legs are visible extending laterally. The texture appears glossy and wet, consistent with a cooked crustacean.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition between the red exoskeleton and the white joint membranes appears slightly soft and 'painted on' rather than having distinct biological segmentation boundaries. Some areas look like smooth gradients rather than textured chitin.
The legs in the bottom left corner seem to merge into each other and the background without clear separation points. The anatomy becomes ambiguous, with potential fusion of limb segments.
The geometry of the right claw seems slightly warped; the pincer mechanism doesn't align perfectly with the wrist joint, suggesting a minor structural inconsistency in the hinge area.
